doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: Dutrey, Jimmy Noone and Chicago nightclubs
summary: They recall Dutrey, who bought property in Chicago, Jimmy Noone playing with them at the Dreamland, and the Deluxe nightclub with Freddie Keppard.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: What was this, uh, fellow named, I think he was a trombonist, too. What was their name, Dutray? Dutray, yeah.

He played over at, uh, uh, Lincoln Garden with us. Yeah, yeah. Yeah, he bought that 49th in, uh, in Michigan. That big, black villain. Well, Margaret, Margaret. That big corner. But he lost it. He passed, you know. Yes, he's dead.
And his brother, Sam, is dead now, too. He played clarinet. Yeah. Uh-huh.
Yeah. Jimmy Newman, is he, where, he's here.
Yeah. He used to play with us at the Cabaret, too. At the Dreamland, yeah.
And then up on, uh, 55th Street.

And there was a bunch over to the Deluxe that worked over there. That's where Freddie, uh, Keppert? Keppert. Keppert was. He was, uh, it was an upstairs nightclub, remember? Uh-huh. Up over to States Theater? Yes.
